Will and Jack coach Karen's cousin (Dan Futterman) on his new gay lifestyle, reminding Will of his own experience of coming out in 1986.
Karen's rival (Minnie Driver) attempts to manipulate Jack; Will and Grace revitalize their friendship with a night of board games.
Jack encounters his former babysitter (guest star Demi Moore) and lapses into childlike behavior. Rosanna Arquette and Leigh-Allyn Baker also guest star.
Will and Jack's transformation of Karen's cousin Barry is complete; Karen duels with Beverly during a silent auction for charity.
Jealous Will spots Barry (Dan Futterman) disappearing with Jack; Karen trades places with Rosario to woo a handsome handyman (Bruno Campos).
Will forms an anti-romance club with Karen and his boss (Gene Wilder).

Karen's search for a roommate leads to a high-maintenance individual, who shares many of her eccentricities; Grace and Jack intervene when Will uses painkillers as a crutch.
Karen hires a somewhat immature divorce attorney (guest star Macaulay Culkin) to oppose Will in court.
When Karen's ex-husband dies, she and her British rival (Minnie Driver) have a contest of wills; Leo (Harry Connick Jr.) is needed in Guatemala.
Karen confronts her ex-husband's mistress before inviting everybody for a ceremony on her yacht; Grace suffers from jealousy after meeting her husband's sexy co-worker.
Will and Jack awake in a precarious position while at sea; Grace discovers love letters in Leo's bag from a female colleague.

Karen invites Grace and Leo to play tennis at her exclusive club, but her fierce playing style drives Grace away.
Jack lands a speaking role opposite James Earl Jones in an off-Broadway play and gives the veteran actor some pointers.
Will takes Leo on shopping sprees and for high tea to help him rekindle his love of the city; Karen coaches Jack for the annual gay spelling bee.
Will takes his mother for an afternoon stroll and bumps into an attractive bachelor (Dylan McDermott); Karen continues her lifelong quest to hunt down hubby-stealing Lorraine.
An unorthodox doctor (Jack Black) gives Karen her annual physical; Jack begs Will to support his decision to become a student nurse.
Will urges Grace to stay in New York so they can spend some time together; Karen strong-arms Jack's nursing teacher into letting him skip class but still make the grade.
Will catches the eye of a female diner after being stood up; Grace bumps into a man (Tom Everett Scott) with whom she once shared a forgettable encounter; Karen runs into her nemesis, Candice Bergen.

A weak bladder forces Will to entrust Grace with his place in line for Barry Manilow tickets; Grace's mother (Debbie Reynolds) cancels their annual mother-daughter shopping trip to have dinner with Jack.

Grace's freeloading sister (Geena Davis) comes to town to launch her latest business enterprise; Karen spurns Lyle (John Cleese), then changes her mind after Lorraine (Minnie Driver) expresses her disapproval.
A rich plastic surgeon (guest star Hal Linden) tries to buy Will's affection; Grace boycotts a new restaurant.
Will's new client (Dave Foley) falls for Jack; Grace and Karen discover hidden money while trying to fix the plumbing in Leo's cabin.
Will is the only single man in a cooking class full of couples, including Jack and his new boyfriend (Dave Foley); Karen's mother (Suzanne Pleshette) asks Grace to decorate her apartment.
Will and Grace begin a business venture selling apartments; Jack runs into his former acting mentor, Zandra; Karen and Lyle (John Cleese) try to renew romance.
Will and Grace try to break up Jack and Stuart (Dave Foley) so they can sell the apartment for a higher price; Karen demands that Lyle (John Cleese) discipline his daughter (Minnie Driver).
Real estate entrepreneurs Will and Grace face formidable competition on the East Side from a lesbian couple (Edie Falco, Chloë Sevigny); John Edward gives Karen some psychic guidance.

Grace advises Will to play hard to get with his new boyfriend (Bobby Cannavale); Jack and Karen despair after learning their favorite TV series will be going off the air.
Will introduces his new boyfriend (Bobby Cannavale) to overly critical Grace; Karen tells Jack that their friendship will change after her wedding.
At Tina's (Lesley Ann Warren) urging, Will tries to find out if there is a new woman in his father's life; Jack's son decides to try out for the high-school cheerleading squad.
On the eve of his graduation from nursing school, Jack turns to Will for help writing his commencement address.
Karen moves her wedding to Las Vegas, where Jennifer Lopez agrees to sing at the ceremony.
Karen recruits Jack to help her get Jennifer Lopez to listen to Karen's new song; Grace takes out her frustration over her cheating husband on Will.
Jack wangles his way into Janet Jackson's (guest starring as herself) performance tour as a backup dancer.
As she attempts to steal doughnuts at an AA meeting, Grace has a surprise reunion with Val (Molly Shannon); Will and Jack attend a gay television focus group meeting.
Grace accuses Will of being too nice to strangers; Jack has trouble at his new company when his co-workers mock him about his Cher doll.
Despite the fact that Will has never had a happy birthday, his new relationship with Vince (Bobby Cannavale) gives him hope that this one will be.
Will convinces Jack to aid a local gay-bookstore owner to save his store from closing.
Will and Grace decide to invite Vince and Nadine (Kristin Davis) over, but they quickly learn that, despite similarities in friendship, they are polar opposites.
After a great date with someone else, Grace comes home to a garbled message from Leo; Karen and Jack try to set each other up, but things go awry.
Will, Grace, Jack and Karen go on a road trip for Grace's getaway weekend, but Jack and Karen hate the car ride and bail on the plan.

Vince's mother cannot make her traditional holiday feast, so Will volunteers to make a special meal, but Vince's mother refuses to give him any credit; Jack gives Vince's sister (Jamie-Lynn DiScala) pointers on keeping secrets.
Will makes the holiday meal.
Grace accidentally breaks a treasured figurine at Will's mother's (Blythe Danner) holiday party and blames it on another guest.
An old classmate (Jeff Goldblum) tries to get revenge on Karen by becoming the president of Walker Inc.; Will and Grace run into Vince and a co-worker while playing hooky from work.
Will is reluctant to bring Vince to a dinner party at his boss's (Lily Tomlin) home, fearing it will scratch his chances of making partner at the firm.
When Scott Woolley (Jeff Goldblum) tries to get Grace to fire Karen by impersonating a restaurant owner, the women plan a trap for him.

Although Grace tries to ignore St. Valentine's Day, she winds up with a hunky greeting-card writer (Ed Burns); Karen's former nemesis (Jeff Goldblum) tries to win her heart by showering her with gifts.

Grace drags Will along on her first date with Nick (Edward Burns); Karen tries to set Jack up on a date with the neighborhood bird enthusiast (Luke Perry), but things don't quite go as she has planned.
When Will agrees to fire Karen's pastry chef, he becomes involved in a love triangle that the baker created.
When Jack convinces Will that they need a change of scenery, they buy an apartment in an up-and-coming gay community.
Will is jealous when his no-nonsense therapist (guest star Sharon Stone) becomes fast friends with Grace.
Grace convinces Karen to attend her father's (Alan Arkin) birthday party; Karen entertains herself by spending time with Martin's friend Burt (Lee Majors).
Grace's near-death experience prompts her to write her will and jolts Will into making a life-altering career choice.
When Will's writing career fizzles, Malcolm (Alec Baldwin) makes him another job offer; Grace's old college flame (Eric Stoltz) gives her a job decorating his new hotel.

Grace contemplates an affair with a married man (Eric Stoltz); Jack begins his new career as a talk-show host; Will continues to hide from Karen the fact that Stan is alive.

Jack learns that Will has never learned how to swim, so he makes it his mission to teach him.
Jack tells Karen he believes she belongs with Stan, not Malcolm (Alec Baldwin).
Jack brings Baby Glenn (Jason Biggs), who gained notoriety in the '80s after being trapped in a hole for days, to Will's charity auction and carnival.
Grace and Will spot her ex-husband, Leo, on their plane to London; Will charms a pair of gay flight attendants into letting Grace into first-class to talk with Leo.

Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is offered a chance to join a popular club. With Dustin Diamond.
A retired teacher with unorthodox methods stimulates the class when he substitutes for their regular teacher.

Jessie and Zack (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar) run for student president, each for different reasons.
Zack's use of a subliminal tape to get Kelly to fall for him has results he never intended.

The pranks between rival schools Bayside and Valley escalate during the week of the city cheerleading finals.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) alien disguise is so believable it attracts a government UFO investigator.

Slater's (Mario Lopez) pet dies while in Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) care.

The gang uses an old radio station in the school basement to hold a marathon. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack's antics get Slater thrown out of driver education classes.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) house party turns into a disaster when his mother's favorite statue is broken. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.

Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) advice line backfires and gets him into trouble with everyone. With Mario Lopez.

Zack makes a surprising discovery about his Native American heritage; Lisa learns her family tree includes a Black American hero of the Underground Railroad; Jessie grapples with guilt over her slave-trading ancestry.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) asks Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to go steady and then falls in love with the school nurse.
Mr. Belding's brother Rod (guest star Edward Blatchford) scores points with the class as a substitute history teacher. With Dennis Haskins and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plots to reunite Slater (Mario Lopez), Mr. Belding (Dennis Haskins) and himself with their feuding sweethearts.
Some underhanded shenanigans are employed to win a glee club competition.
A costume ball sets the stage for Zack and Kelly (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to examine their relationship.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) has a hard time dealing with the fact that Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) has a new boyfriend.
A minor accident sends Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) to the hospital, where he nervously faces the prospect of surgery.

Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to impress a college girl by lying about his age.
The students adopt a new mascot when a stray ball injures a duck in the pond behind the football field.
Jessie's stepbrother Eric arrives from New York and blackmails her, Zack and Slater (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez).

When a girl isn't allowed to try out for the wrestling team, the students band together and protest the decision.

On Bayside's annual "cut school day," Mr. Belding warns Zack that if he is absent one more time he will be suspended.
Lisa and Screech make a "love machine" for their science project.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) latest moneymaking scheme involves a "Girls of Bayside" video-dating tape.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) does everything in her power to break up her father's wedding. With Dustin Diamond.
Everyone gets summer jobs at a fancy beach club and decides to hold Zack's birthday party there.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) promises Mr. Carosi (Ernie Sabella) the gang will win a volleyball game against a rival beach club.
Stacy (Leah Remini) gets confused after she enters a contest at Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) urging and finds that he voted for Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen).
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is in love with Stacy (Leah Remini) but fears she is only interested in her college boyfriend.
Stacy (Leah Remini), in charge of the club for the day, learns her father booked two parties for the same night. With Mario Lopez.
Stacy (Leah Remini) moves out after her father forbids her to see Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar).
The entire gang goes to the mall to obtain U2 tickets and ends up camping out overnight. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
Jessie's father invites everyone to his Palm Springs resort to attend his wedding. With Elizabeth Berkley and Mario Lopez.
Casey Kasem (guest starring as himself) chronicles the rise of the rock group Zack Attack. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
The students are shocked during the Christmas season to discover the new girl working in Mr. Moody's store is homeless.
Zack's family invites Laura and her father home for Christmas.
Lisa (Lark Voorhies) wins a mystery weekend at Mr. Jameson's mansion and invites the gang to participate. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) come to blows when they both fall for the new girl in their senior class.

Slater can't find a way to tell his father that he doesn't want to go to West Point.
Valentine's Day finds the gang at the Max reminiscing about past relationships. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack's plan to encourage the teachers to strike backfires on the students when the Academic Bowl is canceled.
Jeremy and James race a car against a yacht up the New Zealand coast; welcoming a new reasonably-priced car.
Jeremy celebrates the 50th birthday of Jaguar E-type; Richard tests an alternative to the Hummer in South Africa.
Hosts race from Wembley to the San Siro stadium in Milan; Jeremy rides the brand-new Toyota GT86 coupe and singer-songwriter Amy MacDonald is the star in the Reasonably Priced Car.
The guys want to prove that the hatchbacks of their youth were better than modern versions; Hugh Bonneville in the "Reasonably Priced Car."
Richard Hammond tests the Alfa Romeo 4C in Lake Como; James May visits Afghanistan; Jeremy Clarkson travels to Bruges; Tom Hiddleston in the "Reasonably Priced Car."
The guys race from London to Edinburgh, traveling by locomotive, motorbike and a Jaguar XK120.
Finding the perfect car for a seventeen-year-old; a race between a McLaren F1 and a Bugatti Veyron.
Deadly toys in the British Army's arsenal; racing the Royal Mail across the British Isles.

Classic cars are put to the test against modern machines; Brian Johnson.
Jeremy and James set out to create a memorable Volkswagen TV ad; Jay Leno.

Jeremy, Richard and James attempt to save the planet by building their own electric car, and then put their latest "green" creation through the rigors of the new car testing process.
Jeremy and Richard debate which company has made the largest number of great cars; getting caravans to campsites without clogging the roads.
Jeremy travels to Belfast for a test of the Renaultsport Twingo 133, involving a tunnel, a ferry and Ross Kemp; Guy Ritchie.

The guys face rivers and vegetation, drug lords, the effects of high elevation and the world's most perilous highway in the Bolivian rainforest.

Jeremy Clarkson makes a film about the BMW X6 and ends up conducting one of the most expensive road tests in "Top Gear" history; James May drives the new Vauxhall Insignia VXR; Richard Hammond tests the Lexus supercar.
James attempts to drive a Toyota Hilux up an active volcano in Iceland, and The Stig rips up the track in the new Bentley Continental Supersports.
Jeremy, Richard and James find a trio of cars which are equally at home on the racetrack as they are at transporting a family to the store.
The cars put to the test include the Aston Martin Rapide, the Porsche Panamera Turbo and the Maserati Quattroporte in a search for the world's greatest four seat supercar.
Clarkson, Hammond and May battle across Burma in three ancient and barely functioning lorries towards Thailand and their final challenge; to build a bridge over the River Kwai.
The guys investigate whether going motor racing is cheaper than playing golf; guest Slash.
In search of the River Nile's source.
The boys build cool and interesting motor homes before setting off for a holiday weekend in the West country.
A man who has spent years running from his painful past is finally forced to face the fears that haunt him.
An Army lieutenant is determined to have revenge on the Indian tribe responsible for his father's death, despite the fact they now want peace.
A woman finally learns the truth about her son that she hasn't seen in 10 years. Guest star: Agnes Moorehead. With Ward Bond and Robert Horton.
A young married couple is faced with a difficult problem when the husband's first wife, who was presumed dead, joins the wagon train.
Major Adams is forced to come to the rescue of a fast-talking con artist who gets himself into a situation that he can't handle.
Jess is livid when his innocent friend is tried, convicted and hanged for the murders of Doc Webb and Sheriff Kiley.
A priest tries to arrange a meeting with Sitting Bull to talk about a peace treaty.
After a run-in with a traveling prizefighter leaves a mess at the station, Jonesy becomes the man's promoter to help pay the bills at the station.
Slim gets a threatening letter, addressed to his late father, from a man who wants vengeance for the death of his son.
While Jess is away, Slim leases a rough section of land to a former lawman who, unbeknownst to Slim, has hired a bunch of outlaws as his ranch hands.
An actor visits a ghost town where he last appeared with his late wife.
Hardie faces opposition when he tries to investigate a friend's drowning death.
A Wells Fargo employee has been killed and Hardie suspects a boxer.
An incoming stage has problems with a drunken, violent passenger who turns out to be the boxer John L. Sullivan.
Hardie becomes involved with a female Wells Fargo agent.
Hardie gets assigned to protect a diamond salesman carrying a small fortune in gems.
Pearl Harvey's heavily insured dog disappears when she comes to town to entertain the miners.
Hardie suspects murder when a Fargo agent allegedly commits suicide.
Outlaw plots to rob the stage from Yuma.
Hardie helps with a stolen doll.
Hardie tracks down loot from a robbery.
Kitty Thorpe wants Hardie to protect her from her escaped convict husband.
A dog helps Hardie catch a jewel thief.
A woman mine owner won't give Wells Fargo a contract until they are investigated.
A Wells Fargo competitor transfers passengers to his line at gunpoint.
Hardie is offered reward for an outlaw.
Hardie suspects that a female gambler is selling rifles to insurgent Indians.
A prisoner threatens revenge.
After Flint happens on the body of an Indian killed by a soldier, the tribal chief threatens to attack if the guilty party does not confess.
A young man who is determined to avoid becoming a henpecked husband must weigh his love for an overbearing woman.
An old friend of Adams and McCullough joins the wagon train and shares the fact that he has recently discovered a gold mine in the nearby hills.
A riverboat gambler who has committed murder pretends to be a parson traveling with his children. With Ward Bond and Robert Horton.
A man returns from the Civil War to find his home and family destroyed as the result of a feud and heads West to seek his revenge.
An old Indian asks to join the wagon train, so his son can learn the ways of the white man because he believes the Indian way of life is dying.
Major Adams intervenes when a friend's niece becomes romantically involved with a gambler. Guest star: Cesar Romero. With Ward Bond and Robert Horton.
Flint finds the ruins of a farmhouse which was attacked by Indians using guns, not arrows; he later finds the gunrunner who supplied them.
When a group of Scottish people join the wagon train as a protection against Indian attacks, two disparate young people fall in love.
An American Indian, his wife and baby join the wagon train when Major Adams discovers him badly beaten by bigoted white settlers.
A young Indian kidnaps his father's fiancé and forces her to work as revenge against the man who treated his mother badly and caused her suicide.
Wyoming Territory has become the winter battleground for the warring Sioux and Cheyenne, forcing Slim and Jess to close the ranch and relay station.
After a drought and the ending of the stage line, Slim and Jess must join a cattle drive run by a stranger who at first seems impressive, but soon their suspicions are aroused.
When Jess serves as a special deputy to transport a man who's accused of killing his wife, the stagecoach is attacked by a group that's looking for the prisoner.
Aging but beautiful Lily Langford is touring the West, and she arrives in Laramie broke and one step ahead of bill collectors, thanks to her gambler husband.
A shapely woman (Felicia Farr) accuses a local boy (Bruce Dern) of making lurid calls. With David White.
A middle-aged widower (John Larkin) enlists the help of a corrupt medium (Kim Hunter) to contact his dead son.
A farmer (Pat Buttram) brings home a sideshow jar whose curious contents frighten his wife (Collin Wilcox).
A prisoner (Edd Byrnes) convinces a fellow inmate to smuggle him out of prison in another's coffin.
A struggling actor (John Cassavetes) auditioning in London learns an old flame (Gena Rowlands) is wed to the play's backer.
A psychology professor sets the scene for murder when he offers married couples the opportunity to have a spouse killed.
A man (E.G. Marshall) begins to receive letters in the mail predicting the outcome of several future events.
A defense lawyer (James Gregory) tells an arrogant criminologist (Vincent Price) that he made a fatal mistake.
A man (Darryl Hickman) recently released from prison stays with his cellmate's family.
A miserly janitor (Oscar Homolka) keeps the contents of a lost wallet, despite the protests of his wife (Jo Van Fleet).
Freed from prison, a thief (Steven Hill) leads his partner (Steve Brodie) to the mine shaft where he hid their loot.
About to be executed for a crime he didn't commit, a man (Harry Guardino) decides to write his side of the story. With Hugh Marlowe.
A teen (Carol Lynley) devises a scheme to escape the influence of her domineering aunt (Jeanette Nolan).
A lonely woman (Dorothy Stickney) believes she has murdered the man (Fred Graham) who killed her cat.
A prosecutor (Pat Hingle) considering a run for Congress is told that he may have convicted an innocent man.
A man (Joseph Cotten) is trapped in an office with the body of his lover (Christine White) whom he just murdered.
A domineering father (John McIntire) tries to run his adult daughter's (Ann Todd) life. With Philip Reed.
A man tries to prove to his friend that a murderer can escape the police if they can't find a motive.
An elderly maid (Mildred Natwick) leaves the parsonage in search of excitement and adventure in Paris.
A physically small husband (Martin Balsam) goes in pursuit of a 200-pound wife-stealing salesman (Leif Erickson). With Norma Crane.
A woman (Jan Sterling) has problems staying away from the racetrack, and it threatens her marriage. With Karl Swenson.
A couple begins their nightly argument when they are suddenly interrupted by a wanted murderer who keeps them hostage.
A soldier (Jacques Bergerac) returning home with a crippled comrade (Marcel Dalio) falls in love with a beautiful girl.
A woman (Jeanette Nolan) questions a man's (Robert Emhardt) motive for wanting to purchase her house.
A woman (Barbara Bel Geddes) falls in love with another man (Michael Rennie) at her engagement party.
A war correspondent's (Gary Merrill) stories about the post-war trail of an Arab leader suddenly change.
A quartet of elderly women (Estelle Winwood, Ellen Corby, Ida Moore, Elizabeth Patterson) try to gain the attention of a handsome detective (Dennis Morgan).
A curious man investigates his tennis partner, only to discover that her supposedly dead husband is very much alive and well.

A worrier (James Best) becomes fearful when an old friend (Steve Brodie) shows an interest in his wife (Katharine Bard).
A lawyer (Edmon Ryan) spends Christmas Eve trying to reconcile a feuding brother (Richard Waring) and sister (Carmen Mathews).
A man tries to convince the authorities that he knows who committed the latest murder in a series of strangulations, but no one will listen to him.
A woman (Joanna Moore) learns that a winning sweepstakes ticket is in the suit her former husband was buried in. With Steve Forrest and James Gregory.
A crocodile valise becomes a vital clue in tracking down a murderer (Denholm Elliott).
A bank teller (Robert H. Harris) invents a seemingly foolproof plan to come up with a lot of quick cash. With Jerry Paris and Philip Pine.
While traveling in chauffeured car, a woman (Jessica Tandy) with psychic powers hears a voice telling a tragic love story.
A lawyer, soon to become mayor, extends an invitation to a woman who once accused him of embezzlement.
An old, unemployed actor (Herbert Marshall) uses an even older ploy to get a part in a play. With Tom Helmore and Julia Adams.
A couple (Biff McGuire, Cloris Leachman) on a train promise their son money if he doesn't interrupt a cowboy's (Chill Wills) story.
A morgue attendant becomes hysterical when a practical joker pulls the ultimate prank and pretends to be a corpse.
A couple (Richard Kiley, Pat Breslin) falls prey to a crooked policeman (Walter Matthau) and corrupt town officials.
Desperate for an acquittal, a man (Leslie Nielsen) makes a lucrative deal with his defense lawyer (Barry Sullivan).
A woman (Joan Hackett) elicits help from a lawyer (Kevin McCarthy) after receiving threatening phone calls.
A young couple (James MacArthur, Lynn Loring) tries to convince the bride's mother (Gloria Swanson) that their love is sincere.
A thief (Telly Savalas) steals a Rolls-Royce, unaware there is a body in the trunk. With Darren McGavin.
When a man and his wife attempt to do away with an elderly lady, they discover that she is not as senile as they had imagined.
A wealthy dowager is concerned for the welfare of her niece who is married to a man beneath her notice.
An unsuccessful artist (Donnelly Rhodes) accused of bomb threats devises a scheme to steal artworks.
An actor threatened by Satan worshipers agrees to star in a new film as long as no one knows where he goes upon leaving the studio each day.
A frightened embezzler (Steven Hill) stages his own suicide with the help of his double-crossing girlfriend (Joanna Moore).
A man (Norman Lloyd) plots to get away from his wife (Marian Seldes) for a while without her knowing.
A man (Gary Merrill) on the ledge of a New York City hotel threatens suicide after his wife's (Elizabeth Montgomery) death.
